headline: NTSB officials provided the final on scene press briefing tonight on the investigation into the runway excursion of 21 Air Flight 7598 at Miami International Airport on Sunday, which left five people dead and five others injured. The Boeing 767 cargo aircraft overran the end of Runway 30 while landing after a flight from San Juan, Puerto Rico. Investigators said data from the final 30 seconds of the flight data recorder shows the crew released the brakes and increased engine power to a level consistent with initiating a go around for approximately four seconds before reapplying the brakes, which remained applied through the end of the recording. The NTSB expects the on scene phase of the investigation to continue for approximately one week as investigators collect additional evidence and conduct interviews. A preliminary report is expected within 30 days, while the full investigation and final report could take more than a year.

headline: U.S. Southern Command has released video showing Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere (JTF-WHEM) forces interdicting and destroying a floating refueling station allegedly supporting narco-trafficking operations in the Eastern Pacific. According to SOUTHCOM, U.S. forces boarded and cleared the vessel, removed the personnel aboard and transferred them to Ecuadorian authorities before sinking the vessel. Intelligence reportedly linked the refueling station to Los Choneros, an Ecuadorian criminal organization designated by the U.S. as a foreign terrorist organization. This is the second operation of this type. JTF-WHEM conducted a similar interdiction on Aug. 28, when Marines and Sailors operating from USS San Antonio (LPD 17) boarded a suspected floating refueling station, removed those aboard, transferred them to Ecuador and then sank the vessel. The video released by SOUTHCOM today shows what appears to be the USS San Antonio operating nearby. The latest operation is part of an increasingly active U.S.-Ecuadorian campaign targeting the maritime logistics network supporting drug trafficking in the Eastern Pacific.

headline: The IAEA board of governors voted to refer Iran to the UN Security Council over its nuclear "non-compliance," the first such referral in 20 years for failing to meet reporting obligations. The resolution, submitted by Britain, France, Germany and the U.S., passed 23-3 with 8 abstentions. Russia, China and Niger voted against. The IAEA has been denied access to key Iranian nuclear facilities since the June 2025 conflict and again after the war that erupted February 28. The move is seen as largely symbolic, as Russia and China can veto any Security Council sanctions. - AFP
